full_qat_frontier_attempt.note: No clean torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError was raised. Instead, VRAM usage climbed to ~94% of the 6.14GB card and plateaued there (5740->5746 MiB over ~4 additional minutes of observation), with GPU utilization pinned at 100% but power draw only ~26W -- far below genuine compute load. This is the same Windows CUDA driver shared-memory-fallback pattern already documented for Qwen2.5-0.5B eval on Day 5 (docs/reports/2026-08-30_session-5.md; docs/MATH.md sec 2): high utilization from the driver repeatedly retrying/paging, not real forward progress. Killed manually after 17 minutes with zero training steps completed (the probe has no per-step logging, so this was confirmed via nvidia-smi memory/utilization/power trend, not inferred from silence). This is treated as the experiments intended failure result (the docstring: attempt_full_qat is expected to OOM or come very close -- that failure IS the result), just manifesting as an indefinite silent slowdown rather than a clean exception on this Windows/consumer-GPU setup, consistent with and extending the projects existing VRAM-oversubscription finding to the training side of a genuinely oversized (1.1B param) model.
